definition: Predicting the per-pixel surface orientation of a scene — a mid-level 3D cue used for shading, robotics, and scene understanding.
details: Predicting the per-pixel surface orientation of a scene — a mid-level 3D cue used for shading, robotics, and scene understanding.

explainer.lead: Surface normals estimation predicts each pixel's surface orientation, giving a mid-level 3D cue about scene geometry. It matters because shading, robotics, and scene understanding all build on that orientation information.

tiers.eli5: For every spot in a picture, it guesses which way the surface there is facing, like knowing which way each panel of a crumpled sheet points.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use predicted normals as an intermediate representation feeding shading, robotics, and scene understanding. The pitfall is that per-pixel predictions can be locally plausible yet inconsistent as a whole surface.
tiers.paperLevel: Predicting per-pixel surface orientation of a scene as a mid-level 3D cue. Being mid-level, it is an intermediate estimate rather than full 3D reconstruction.

explainer.example: Producing a normal map for an indoor photo so a renderer can compute shading from the estimated orientations.
